corrections.text: The article states that "border officers said they were demanding access to his phone 'under the pretext of searching for child exploitation imagery'." TechCrunch's reporting actually attributes this framing to an accusation made by Tunick's attorneys against the government, not to a statement by the officers themselves: "Tunick's attorneys accused the government of demanding access to his phone under the pretext of searching for child exploitation imagery, but without providing evidence to justify its suspicion."
The article names the Electronic Frontier Foundation technologist quoted as "Bill Buddington." The correct spelling, per TechCrunch, is "Bill Budington."
